notes.text: The page is headed Exercice 4.10.6. It assumes a U-site S with topology no finer than the canonical one, and an underlined class M of arrows satisfying conditions a–d: quarrability and base-change stability; identities and composition; locality on a covering family of the target; and covering refinements with arrows in M. This is an account of the source's assertions only.
notes.basis: Observation: opening and conditions a–d. No theorem verification was performed.

notes.text: The definition names S(X), double-quoted petit site de X, using the full subcategory of S/X whose structural maps lie in M and the induced topology. The source replaces the cancelled considérons le site with notons, and replaces dont la catégorie sous-jacente est with constitué par; le site is supplied in the left margin. The acute on é in considérons is visible.
notes.basis: Observation: definition and crops 04–05; the marginal insertion is observed in half a. No grammatical normalisation or proof inference.

notes.text: Question 1 asks that the indicated covering families form a pretopology generating S's topology. The epsilon-shaped sign in the indexing is transcribed as printed, without replacing it by a membership sign on mathematical grounds.

Question 2 asks for continuity of base change from S(Y) to S(X), then introduces S(u)^* between the corresponding categories of sheaves. The star and superscript tildes are pen completions. The source has the closing reference (III 1.2,iv)). with two closing parentheses.
notes.basis: Observation: question 2 and half b. The arrows and superscript positions were read from the ink, not proved correct.

notes.text: Question 3 begins an equivalence between the topos S with superscript tilde and systems (F_X), (varphi_u). It gives objects in S(X) with superscript tilde and a morphism varphi_u:S(u)^*(F_Y) to F_X. The text ends on this page at ces systèmes; no continuation has been supplied.
notes.basis: Observation: question 3, crops 08–09, and bottom margin.

notes.text: No date or authorial page number is visible. The pencilled 9 in the lower-left corner is retained as an archive comment.

notes.text: The opening handwritten M is legible, with an uncertain S-shaped typed underprint. Conditions a and b have S/M superpositions whose strike order remains unresolved. The initial of On notera has two rounded contours: repeated O or O/o replacement remains possible. The source spelling quarrables and doubled closing parenthesis are retained.
notes.basis: Main crops 01–03 and 06 from r1; three full readings for prose and punctuation.

notes.text: Targeted check of item 1: identities are in the class by (b), and isomorphisms are base changes of identities. Condition (a) supplies pullbacks and stability of the class; (b) supplies composition stability. The site axioms keep the resulting families covering. Condition (d) refines every original covering family by one of these families, so the generated topology is the original topology. Condition (c) is not needed for this limited check. This argument does not decide any disputed glyph.
notes.basis: Main-reader reasoning using the stated conditions a, b, d and item 1; detailed working in decisions/scan010_math_work.md.
notes.event_outcome: Checked the pretopology closure conditions and equality of generated topology by refinement, as stated in note s010-note08. This is a limited mathematical argument for item 1, not a proof of the whole exercise.

notes.text: Limited type check for item 2: if u:X→Y and Z→Y is an object of S(Y), condition (a) provides Z×_Y X→X in S(X). This supports the direction S(Y)→S(X). Continuity and the equivalence begun in item 3 were not independently proved here.

notes.event_outcome: Checked existence and membership in the designated class of the pulled-back structural arrow, hence the direction of the object assignment. Did not establish the full continuity or equivalence assertions.
